families.intro: Motion is the oldest special effect. Ceilings that breathe, sculptures that turn, rails that ripple under a hand. Engineered movement is felt before it is understood, and it is the one thing a screen can never do.

cats.name: KINETIC CEILINGS & CANOPIES
cats.blurb: The overhead gesture that makes a whole space feel engineered and alive.

entries.name: KINETIC CEILING FIELD
entries.line: A sky of suspended elements that rise, fall and gather into formations above your guests.
entries.moment: Visitors walk in and feel the ceiling first. Hundreds of elements drift at different heights, pull together into a wave or a slow bowl, then release. It stays calm through the quiet hours and turns theatrical on cue for a reveal, a keynote or a royal arrival.
entries.best: Atriums · Exhibition zones · Launch events · Experience centres

entries.name: THE BLOOM
entries.line: Giant kinetic flowers that open overhead, petals unfolding around a heart of light.
entries.moment: Closed, they hang like sculptural buds. On cue, as a guest arrives, a product is unveiled or the clock strikes, layered petals open to more than four metres across and the room changes colour with them. Then they fold, and wait for the next moment.
entries.best: Hotel & mall atriums · Gala dinners · Product launches · Seasonal installations

entries.name: BLADE CANOPY
entries.line: Rows of luminous blades tilt in travelling waves, carrying colour and content across the ceiling.
entries.moment: Look up and the ceiling is combing itself. Long blades of light tilt one after another, so a wave of colour rolls from the entrance to the stage and back again. It can idle like slow breathing, follow the music, or snap flat into one clean surface the moment a speaker walks on.
entries.best: Atriums · Exhibition halls · Launch events · Hospitality lobbies

entries.name: FACET CANOPY
entries.line: A field of light-up triangles that fold and unfold into faceted patterns overhead.
entries.moment: Overhead, a field of glowing triangles folds like slow origami. Flat, it is a calm luminous ceiling. Then facets tip and catch the light, ridges and valleys travel across it, and the canopy settles into a new landscape. Colour and movement are composed together, so it can mark the hours, a brand moment or the start of the show.
entries.best: Lobbies · Retail atriums · Pavilions · Gala dinners

entries.name: SPHERE DRIFT
entries.line: Glowing spheres rise and fall on invisible lines to draw shapes, logos and slow weather in the air.
entries.moment: Hundreds of glowing spheres hang in the air like a held breath. One by one they rise and fall until a shape appears: a wave, a dune line, a falcon's wing, your emblem in three dimensions. Between moments they drift like slow weather, which is reason enough to stop and watch.
entries.best: Atriums · Airports & malls · Brand pavilions · Opening ceremonies

entries.name: THE MURMURATION
entries.line: A constellation of polished metal spheres performs one slow bow as guests arrive, then resettles. No screens, only engineered grace.
entries.moment: Guests step into the hall and the ceiling acknowledges them. A cloud of mirror-polished spheres dips in one slow, continuous bow, holds for a breath, then rises and resettles into stillness. There is nothing to read and nothing to touch. It is a gesture of welcome, performed with the precision of a watch.
entries.best: Experience centres · VIP arrivals · Headquarters · Museums

entries.name: SWARM LIGHT
entries.line: Hundreds of small lights behave like a flock, drifting, gathering and releasing. For spaces where moving parts don't belong.
entries.moment: Nothing moves, yet the ceiling is alive. Hundreds of small points of light behave like a flock: they drift across the space, gather above a group of guests, scatter, and regroup somewhere else. It gives a room the feeling of kinetic art with no moving parts, so it suits heritage buildings, low ceilings and spaces that never close.
entries.best: Heritage buildings · Lounges · Corridors · Restaurants & hotels

entries.name: DEPTH CEILING
entries.line: A screen ceiling designed with forced perspective, so the roof appears to open into another world.
entries.moment: The roof seems to have been removed. Above the guests a shaft of architecture climbs into open sky, clouds pass, a falcon crosses, night falls and the stars come out. The picture is composed for the way people actually stand beneath it, which is what makes a flat ceiling read as real depth.
entries.best: Entrance halls · Malls · Hotel lobbies · Themed attractions

entries.name: HALO RINGS
entries.line: Illuminated rings float and turn overhead, each on its own height, speed and colour, drawing slow shapes in the air.
entries.moment: Rings of light hang above the room at different heights. They rise, tilt and turn on their own motors, each in its own colour, so the ceiling draws slow three-dimensional figures: a spiral that unwinds during dinner, one flat plane for the speech, a storm of colour for the reveal. It belongs where a chandelier would be expected and something better arrives.
entries.best: Gala dinners · Luxury lounges · Hotel atriums · Brand pavilions

entries.name: LIGHT TUBES
entries.line: Tubes of light rise, fall and spin on motorised lines, in time with the music or the film.
entries.moment: A hundred slim tubes of light hang from motorised winches. They lift and lower in waves, spin to throw their beams around the room, and change colour with the music, so the ceiling becomes a light show with a body to it. Programmed once, it can idle as a slow tide all evening and wake for the moment that matters.
entries.best: Concerts & award nights · Product reveals · Stage backdrops · Atriums

entries.name: PIXEL CANOPY
entries.line: A ceiling of square screens that rise and tilt, so the picture overhead has depth as well as motion.
entries.moment: Above the floor hangs a grid of square screens, each on its own lift. Together they show one picture, a sky, a sea, a map, and as the picture moves the panels move with it: a wave lifts the screens as it passes, a spotlight sinks one panel towards the person beneath. The roof of the room becomes a surface that thinks in three dimensions.
entries.best: Exhibition stands · Showrooms · Lobbies · Launch events

cats.name: KINETIC SCULPTURES & MOVING SCREENS
cats.blurb: Landmarks that turn, slide and breathe. The pieces people navigate by and photograph.

entries.name: THE HELIX
entries.line: A tower of stacked rotating rings wrapped in screens. A brand story that literally turns.
entries.moment: From across the hall it reads as a twisting column of light. Each level rotates on its own, so images spiral upward, align into one tall canvas, then break apart again. It becomes the landmark people meet beside and the picture they take home.
entries.best: Exhibition stands · Lobbies · Launch stages · Malls

entries.name: TIDE WALL
entries.line: A wall of screens that physically moves, columns rising and falling like a tide while the picture flows across them.
entries.moment: At rest it is a clean media wall. Then the surface itself starts to move: columns lift and sink in slow waves, a doorway opens in the middle, a logo pushes forward in relief. The content and the choreography are written together, so picture and motion feel like one material.
entries.best: Stage backdrops · Corporate lobbies · Stands · Showrooms

entries.name: MIRROR HELIX
entries.line: A compact twisting tower with two faces, screen and mirror, that flips between showing your content and reflecting the room.
entries.moment: One moment it is a column of moving image, the next it is a column of mirror, throwing the room and the people in it back at themselves. Each tier turns on its own, so picture and reflection spiral around each other. It is compact enough for a stand and restless enough to be seen from across the hall.
entries.best: Exhibition stands · Showrooms · Retail · Hotel lobbies

entries.name: SLIDING GALLERY
entries.line: Twenty tall screens glide along a rail, parting and regrouping to form one image, many images, or a doorway.
entries.moment: A row of tall screens that will not stay still. They slide together into a single panorama, drift apart into a gallery of separate portraits, then part in the middle to let a speaker, a car or a guest of honour walk through. The film is written for the movement, so every regrouping lands on a beat.
entries.best: Stages · Launches · Showrooms · Corporate lobbies

entries.name: PULSE SPHERE
entries.line: A sphere built from screen panels that push out and draw back, so the whole globe appears to breathe.
entries.moment: A globe of screens hangs at the heart of the space, and it breathes. Panels push outward and draw back in waves, so the surface swells like a living planet while the picture wraps around it. It can be the Earth, a data sphere, a pearl or a pure pulse of colour, readable from every side.
entries.best: Atriums · Exhibition stands · Sustainability & tech pavilions · Lobbies

entries.name: PRISM COLUMN
entries.line: Three stacked triangular sections rotate independently. Nine faces, nine chapters, endless combinations.
entries.moment: Three triangular drums stand one on top of another, every face a screen. They turn independently: sometimes aligning into one tall image, sometimes offering three different stories to three sides of the room. Nine faces give you nine chapters, and the turning itself tells people that something new is about to appear.
entries.best: Exhibition stands · Malls · Lobbies · Product launches

entries.name: THE EMBLEM
entries.line: Your symbol as a double-sided sculptural screen, turning a full 360 degrees.
entries.moment: Your symbol, built at the scale of a sculpture and alive with moving image on both faces. It turns slowly through a full circle, so the whole hall sees it, and the content is cut to its outline instead of to a rectangle. Visitors photograph it the way they would a landmark.
entries.best: Exhibition stands · Headquarters lobbies · National occasions · Anniversaries

entries.name: STROKE ARRAY
entries.line: A cluster of small screens on moving arms that tilt and pivot together to trace shapes: calligraphic strokes, logos, waves.
entries.moment: A cluster of small screens on slender arms, moving like a single hand. Together they tilt and pivot to trace a shape in the air: the sweep of a calligraphic stroke, the curve of a wave, the outline of a mark. The image flows across them as they move, so gesture and picture are one performance.
entries.best: Biennales & art fairs · Cultural pavilions · Lobbies · Launch stages

entries.name: ORBIT SCREENS
entries.line: Screens revolve around a product or model, revealing a new layer of the story from every angle.
entries.moment: The object stays still at the centre: a car, a model, an artefact. Screens circle it like satellites, and whatever they pass in front of, they explain. From one side a visitor sees the skin, from another the structure beneath, from a third the story of how it was made.
entries.best: Automotive · Museums · Real-estate models · Product launches

entries.name: THE FLOAT
entries.line: A product hovering and slowly turning in mid-air with nothing holding it. Quiet, and impossible to walk past.
entries.moment: A single product hovers above its plinth, turning slowly, with nothing above it and nothing beneath it. People stop, look for the wire, and pass a hand through the gap. It is the quietest piece in the catalogue and one of the most effective, because the only thing on show is the product itself.
entries.best: Luxury retail · Fragrance & jewellery · Launch plinths · Shop windows

entries.name: LIVING RELIEF
entries.line: A mural of thousands of physical discs that flip in soft waves, redrawing pattern, portrait and calligraphy with the sound of rain.
entries.moment: A wall made of thousands of small discs, dark on one side and bright on the other. They flip in soft waves and the mural redraws itself: a geometric pattern, a portrait, a line of calligraphy, the silhouette of whoever is standing in front of it. Every change arrives with a sound like rain on a roof.
entries.best: Lobbies · Cultural centres · Museums · Headquarters

entries.name: BREATHING SCREEN
entries.line: A lattice of apertures opens and closes in slow waves, turning daylight into moving geometry across the floor.
entries.moment: A patterned screen in the tradition of the mashrabiya, except that this one moves. Its apertures open and close in slow waves, and the daylight that falls through them travels across the floor as living geometry. It shades the space through the day and performs at the hours you choose.
entries.best: Façades & atriums · Cultural buildings · Hospitality · Majlis spaces

entries.name: PRECISION SKIN
entries.line: A wall of thousands of small moving elements. Calm at a distance, alive up close, rippling around whoever stands nearest.
entries.moment: From across the room it is a calm, finely textured wall. Walk closer and it notices: thousands of small machined elements tilt towards you and a ripple follows you along its length. Step away and it settles. It is a feature wall with the manners of a living thing, built to be looked at for years.
entries.best: Headquarters · Experience centres · Luxury retail · Hotel lobbies

entries.name: KINETIC WINGS
entries.line: Wings of light along the edge of the stand fold and unfold in choreographed waves.
entries.moment: Along the border of the stand, pairs of light strips are hinged like wings. They fold shut, open wide and ripple in sequence, so the whole edge of the space beats slowly like something alive. From across the hall it is the first thing people see; up close, each wing carries its own colour and pattern. It marks a territory without a single wall.
entries.best: Exhibition stands · Stage edges · Retail façades · Festival gateways

entries.name: THE ARMILLARY
entries.line: Rings of screen orbit a glowing sphere, each turning on its own, like an instrument for reading the sky.
entries.moment: A sphere of light at the centre, and around it three rings of screen that revolve independently, tilting through each other like an antique instrument for measuring the heavens. Content flows around the rings and across the globe, so a brand story can be told in orbits: the product at the heart, its world turning around it.
entries.best: Exhibition centrepieces · Museums · Science & energy pavilions · Lobbies

entries.name: THE RING PORTAL
entries.line: A four-metre ring of screen you walk up to or through, steered with a single dial.
entries.moment: A great ring of screen stands upright on the floor, tall enough to walk through. On its face, chapters float past; turn the brass dial on the plinth and the ring answers with the film for the chapter you chose, wrapping the picture around its curve. Visitors step through it to enter the next zone, so the gateway is also the first exhibit.
entries.best: Exhibition entrances · Pavilions · Retail · Career fairs

entries.name: KINETIC PILLAR
entries.line: A column whose screen panels push out and draw back in patterns, the picture moving with them.
entries.moment: From a distance it is a column wrapped in screen. Then the panels begin to move: rows push outward, neighbours draw back, and a pattern travels up the pillar while the content on its faces follows the motion. It can stand at the centre of a stand or dress a lobby's structural column, turning something you would walk past into something you walk around.
entries.best: Exhibition stands · Lobbies · Malls · Showrooms

entries.name: THE UNFOLDING CUBE
entries.line: A cube whose tiers rise, spread and turn: a mechanical reveal for a launch.
entries.moment: A closed cube of screen sits on the stage. At the cue, its tiers lift on hydraulic columns, spread apart and begin to turn, each level carrying its own picture, until the cube has opened like a mechanical flower around whatever was hidden inside. For launches it is a reveal; between shows it settles back into a quiet, turning sculpture.
entries.best: Product launches · Stage moments · Exhibition centrepieces · Auto shows

entries.name: FLOATING DOME
entries.line: A hemisphere of screen hanging in the atrium: a planet, a sky, a world seen from below.
entries.moment: A dome of screen hangs over the hall with its open face turned to the floor, so that everyone beneath it looks up into a bowl of picture: a planet turning, a night sky, a coral reef, a city seen from a cloud. It fills the volume of an atrium the way no flat screen can, and from the balconies it reads as a sculpture.
entries.best: Atriums · Museums · Planetarium moments · Event halls

entries.name: MIRROR WALL
entries.line: Columns of turning panels, screen on one face and mirror on the other, that switch from picture to reflection and back.
entries.moment: A wall built from tall columns, each column a stack of panels that pivot on a vertical axis. One face is screen, the other is mirror. As the panels turn, the wall changes from one seamless picture into a broken field of reflections and back, waves of mirror rolling across the image. A dial on the podium lets a visitor choose the chapter, and the wall rearranges itself to show it.
entries.best: Exhibition stands · Retail · Hotel lobbies · Fashion events

entries.name: SCREEN ATLAS
entries.line: A map of the world, or of your sites, built from screens of many sizes, each a window into a place.
entries.moment: The continents are drawn in screens: dozens of displays of different sizes and orientations, arranged so their outline is the world map, or your country, or your network of sites. Each screen is a window into one place, and the whole wall moves as one when the story calls for it. It suits any organisation whose story is where it is.
entries.best: Corporate lobbies · Trade shows · Airlines, ports & logistics · Real estate

cats.name: ROBOTICS
cats.blurb: Precision machines with stage presence. Robots that perform, film, draw and serve.

entries.name: ROBOTIC REVEAL
entries.line: Industrial robot arms dance screens or a product through the air, in perfect time with the film.
entries.moment: The lights drop and the machines begin to move. Two arms carry their screens through a choreographed duet, framing the product, handing the picture from one to the other, freezing on the beat. It is a launch film and a live performance at once, repeatable to the millisecond, show after show.
entries.best: Product launches · Auto & tech reveals · Opening ceremonies

entries.name: HERO CAM
entries.line: A robot arm swings a high-speed camera around your guests and hands back a slow-motion, film-star moment in seconds.
entries.moment: Guests step onto the mark, strike a pose, and the arm sweeps past in a move no human operator could repeat. Moments later the clip arrives on their phone: graded, branded and ready to post. The queue becomes part of the show.
entries.best: Galas · Premieres · Brand activations · Weddings & VIP events

entries.name: THE DRAWING ARM
entries.line: A robot that sketches portraits, patterns or signatures live, stroke by stroke, while a crowd gathers to watch.
entries.moment: A guest sits, the arm picks up its pen, and the portrait appears in one confident line after another. Nobody can watch a robot draw for less than a minute, so a crowd forms around every sitting. The guest leaves with an original on paper, drawn by the machine and dressed in your brand.
entries.best: Brand activations · Exhibitions · Hospitality events · Retail openings

entries.name: SCANNER ARM
entries.line: A robot sweeps a screen across a real object and reveals what is inside it, x-ray style: an engine, an anatomy, the layers of a city.
entries.moment: A robot arm carries a screen slowly across a real object, and wherever the screen passes, the inside is revealed: the engine beneath the bodywork, the structure inside the tower, the layers beneath the city. Visitors choose what to inspect from a touch podium, and the arm travels there for them.
entries.best: Automotive · Energy & industry · Museums · Medical & science

entries.name: ROBOT HOST
entries.line: A robot arm pours the coffee, mixes the drink or hands over the gift, styled to your brand and choreographed to charm.
entries.moment: The most talked-about member of the hospitality team is the one made of metal. The arm lifts the dallah and pours Arabic coffee with a flourish, mixes a mocktail, or picks up a gift and presents it with a small bow. Every movement is choreographed for charm, and the queue films all of it.
entries.best: Hospitality lounges · Exhibition stands · Retail openings · VIP gifting

entries.name: THE CARVING ARM
entries.line: A robot sculpts live from a block, a form emerging in front of the crowd, stroke by stroke.
entries.moment: A block of foam on a turntable, a robot arm with a cutting head, and a crowd that stops. Over an hour the block becomes a form: an anatomical heart, a landmark, your product, a portrait bust. Finished pieces line the stand as the day's gallery. It is the same fascination as watching a potter, at industrial scale.
entries.best: Medical & science exhibitions · Auto & engineering stands · Museums · Launches

entries.name: THE CAROUSEL
entries.line: A turntable of real objects; choose one and it turns to face you while a robot and the screen tell its story.
entries.moment: Around a circular table sit the real things: a turbine blade, a bottle, a model of a building, a piece of the product. Choose one on the tablet and the table turns until it stops in front of you; the robot arm at the centre picks up its story, gesturing, lifting, presenting, while the screen behind fills in the detail. A showcase that explains itself, one object at a time.
entries.best: Industrial & energy stands · Product showcases · Museums · Investor centres

cats.name: LIVING ARCHITECTURE
cats.blurb: Rails, doors, walls and benches that notice people, and answer the hand.

entries.name: THE LIVING RAIL
entries.line: Handrails and balustrades that ripple with light or motion under a visitor's hand.
entries.moment: It reads as a premium rail until someone touches it. Then a current of light gathers around their hand and follows them up the stair. In its mechanical form, small machined segments tilt in a wave just ahead of them. Technology stops being a screen and becomes the building noticing you.
entries.best: Experience centres · Headquarters · Museums · Pavilions

entries.name: PERFORMING ROOM FRONTS
entries.line: Meeting-room and studio façades whose panels slide and reveal on cue, so every door announces what is happening inside.
entries.moment: Along the corridor, every room has a face. Panels slide, turn and open on cue, so a studio announces that a session is starting, a meeting room closes itself for privacy, and a whole street of doors wakes in sequence when a delegation arrives. The architecture does the hosting.
entries.best: Experience centres · Innovation hubs · Headquarters · Studios & academies

entries.name: IRIS THRESHOLD
entries.line: One doorway that performs its opening, blades or rings parting in sequence, for the entrance that deserves ceremony.
entries.moment: Some rooms deserve an entrance. As guests approach, the doorway performs: curved blades part in sequence like the iris of a great camera, light spills through the widening circle, and the room beyond is revealed at the pace of a curtain rising. Behind them it closes again, and the sense of occasion stays.
entries.best: VIP suites · Museum galleries · Experience centres · Boardrooms

entries.name: PATHFINDER MARKERS
entries.line: Floor lights brighten ahead of visitors and dim behind them. Wayfinding that feels like attention rather than signage.
entries.moment: No arrows and no signs. Small markers of light set into the floor brighten a few steps ahead of each visitor and fade behind them, so the route appears as they walk it. A host can send a delegation's path ahead of them, and at night the markers settle into a slow, quiet pulse.
entries.best: Experience centres · Museums · Campuses · Hospitality

entries.name: LIGHT GATE
entries.line: An arrival arch that senses guests and sweeps light around its frame as they pass beneath.
entries.moment: An arch that knows when someone walks through it. As each guest passes beneath, a sweep of light races around the frame and settles again, so every arrival gets a small moment of ceremony. For the opening it can count guests in, change colour for a VIP, or run as one continuous show.
entries.best: Event entrances · Festivals · Retail openings · Exhibition gateways

entries.name: GEAR WALL
entries.line: Magnetic gears, one crank, one bell. Build the chain true and the whole wall turns.
entries.moment: A steel wall, a box of magnetic gears in every size, one crank at one end and one bell at the other. Children and engineers work side by side to build a chain that carries the turn all the way across. When the last gear meshes, the whole wall comes alive and the bell rings. No screens, no instructions needed.
entries.best: Children's museums · Science centres · Family zones · Schools programmes

entries.name: CURIOSITY BENCH
entries.line: Hands-on instruments to crank, spin and pump, where a visitor's own effort makes light, air and motion happen. No screens at all.
entries.moment: A long workbench of beautifully made instruments, each asking to be cranked, spun or pumped. Turn a handle and a lamp glows by your own effort. Pump, and a column of air lifts a ball. Spin a wheel and colours blend to white. Every station teaches one idea in ten seconds, and there is not a screen in sight.
entries.best: Science centres · Children's galleries · Education programmes · Family zones

cats.name: ARCADE & MECHANICAL GAMES
cats.blurb: Levers, claws, pedals and photo finishes. Play you can hear from across the hall.

entries.name: THE CAMEL DERBY
entries.line: A loud, joyful mechanical race. Six lanes, six sculpted racers, one winner: camels, horses, cars or your own mascot.
entries.moment: Pick your camel, grip the lever, hold your breath. The camels glide down their lanes while a dune-shaped scoreboard counts them home and the crowd picks sides. A race takes ninety seconds, anyone can play, and it is the noisiest corner of the festival in the best way.
entries.best: National celebrations · Festivals · Family zones · Brand activations

entries.name: TREASURE CLAW
entries.line: A glowing pool of treasures and a claw to fish them out. The arcade game everyone already knows how to play, dressed in your story.
entries.moment: A glowing pool of treasures beneath glass, a claw above it, and one joystick. Everyone already knows how to play. Each capsule that comes up carries a prize, a piece of your story or a golden ticket. The cabinet is crafted around your theme, never like a fairground machine: for a heritage festival it becomes a pearling dhow in timber, rope and brass.
entries.best: National celebrations · Heritage festivals · Malls · Brand activations

entries.name: GIANT CONTROLLER
entries.line: A metre-high joystick and two dome buttons. It takes two people to play well, which is the point.
entries.moment: A joystick as tall as a child and two dome buttons the size of dinner plates, facing a big screen. One person cannot reach everything, so strangers become a team within seconds: one steers with both arms, the other jumps on the buttons. It turns any simple game into physical comedy, and the crowd enjoys it as much as the players.
entries.best: Family zones · Festivals · Gaming events · Brand activations

entries.name: ARCADE DUO
entries.line: Two classic arcade cabinets, head to head, dressed in your colours, with a daily high-score board.
entries.moment: Two classic upright cabinets, side by side and head to head, dressed in your colours from marquee to control panel. Pick a well-loved style of game, put the day's best scores on a board above, and the rivalry runs itself. It is one of the quickest pieces here to deliver, and it never stands empty.
entries.best: Office & campus events · Exhibition stands · Retail · Lounges

entries.name: CUSTOM CABINET
entries.line: Your own title in your own machine. We design the game, the artwork and the cabinet around your brand.
entries.moment: A game that exists nowhere else, in a machine built only for it. We design the play around your story, draw the artwork, shape the cabinet and its controls, and tune the difficulty so the first go is easy and the high score is hard. After the event it moves to your reception, and keeps working.
entries.best: Brand launches · Flagship stores · Headquarters · Touring activations

entries.name: KINETIC MAZE
entries.line: A giant tilting labyrinth steered with one oversized joystick.
entries.moment: The wooden labyrinth game from childhood, grown to the size of a dining table. One oversized joystick tilts the whole board, and a steel ball has to be coaxed past the holes to the finish. It is a test of patience played in front of an audience, and everybody in the queue believes they can do better.
entries.best: Exhibition stands · Family zones · Team events · Malls

entries.name: PEDAL POWER
entries.line: Bikes that drive the content. The harder the crowd pedals, the further the story goes.
entries.moment: A row of bikes facing a big screen, and nothing on it moves until somebody pedals. Legs drive the race, light the city or fill the bottle, and the harder the team works the further the story goes. It turns energy, sustainability and teamwork into something you feel in your legs.
entries.best: Sustainability & energy stands · Sports events · Team days · Malls

entries.name: REFLEX WALL
entries.line: Lights flash, hands fly. A speed-and-reflex challenge with a leaderboard that keeps people coming back.
entries.moment: A wall of lights and thirty seconds on the clock. Targets flash, hands fly, and the score climbs with every hit. One round takes half a minute and explains itself, which keeps the queue moving, and the leaderboard above brings the same people back all day to take their place again.
entries.best: Sports & automotive brands · Exhibition stands · Malls · Team events

entries.name: STRENGTH TEST
entries.line: The fairground hammer, rebuilt in your brand's light, sound and colour.
entries.moment: The fairground classic: swing the hammer and watch the light race up the tower towards the bell. We rebuild it in your colours with its own sound and light show, and set the levels to suit the day, from family fun to a serious contest with a prize at the top.
entries.best: Festivals · Family days · Sports brands · Outdoor activations

entries.name: STEP DUEL
entries.line: Two players, two strips of light-up tiles, first to the end wins.
entries.moment: Two lanes of light-up tiles, two players, one countdown. Stamp on each tile as it lights and your lane advances; miss one and your rival pulls ahead. A duel lasts twenty seconds and is as much fun to watch as to play, so it suits the busiest corner of the floor.
entries.best: Malls · Retail activations · Family zones · Sports events

entries.name: GIANT SNAKES & LADDERS
entries.line: The board game at room scale, with a huge dice and a digital surprise on every square.
entries.moment: The board covers the floor, the players are the pieces, and the dice needs two hands to throw. Land on a ladder and you climb; land on a snake and the whole room groans. Every square can carry a question, a fact or a small prize, so the message is learned by playing.
entries.best: Family days · Schools programmes · Malls · Community festivals

entries.name: TABLE FOOTBALL
entries.line: Table football with your players, your pitch and your tactics.
entries.moment: A table everyone knows how to play, rebuilt around your brand: your colours on the players, your pitch, your name on the scoreboard. A stretched edition seats eight at once, with goals counted in light and sound. It draws the people who would never queue for a screen.
entries.best: Sports sponsorships · Fan zones · Office events · Hospitality lounges

entries.name: THE THROW WALL
entries.line: Throw real balls at a projected wall that reacts: targets, goals and quick games for a queue.
entries.moment: Soft balls in a basket and a wall that plays back. Throw, and the target bursts where the ball lands; hit the right shape and the score climbs; two players race to clear the wall. Games change through the day, and the wall can wear any world: a fortress, a rainforest, a football goal, your product's own landscape. Nobody needs instructions.
entries.best: Family zones · Sports events · Malls · Team days

entries.name: LED PITCH
entries.line: Football on a sensor floor: the pitch reads the players' feet and plays along.
entries.moment: A floor of screen marked out as a pitch, and a game that knows where every foot is. The ball on the floor is light; kick it and it flies, goals flash, the crowd on the boards roars. Five-a-side in a space the size of a living room, with replays and a leaderboard on the wall. Built for sports brands, fan zones and the energetic end of a family day.
entries.best: Fan zones · Sports brands · Malls · Schools & youth events

entries.name: MIND RACE
entries.line: Slot cars driven by concentration alone, through a headset that reads how hard you focus.
entries.moment: Two lanes, two cars, no controllers. Each racer wears a light headset that reads their concentration; the calmer and more focused they are, the faster their car goes. Lose your focus and it slows. The crowd shouts, which makes it harder, which makes it funnier. A race that rewards exactly the quality most brands want to talk about.
entries.best: Tech & education exhibitions · Wellness brands · Team days · Malls

entries.name: PEDAL RACERS
entries.line: Slot cars around a model of your city, powered by how hard the players pedal.
entries.moment: A model landscape on a table, a race track winding through it, and two bikes beside it. The harder you pedal, the faster your car goes past the landmarks; the first around the circuit wins. The city can be yours, the cars can be your fleet, and the leaderboard runs all day. A physical race that gets adults competing as hard as children.
entries.best: Auto & mobility brands · Tourism · Family zones · Sports events

entries.name: THE PASS GAME
entries.line: Six joysticks around a floor of light; keep the balls in play together as they speed up.
entries.moment: Six players stand around a floor of screen, each with a joystick and a glowing bar to defend. Balls of light bounce between them, more arrive, and every twenty seconds they get faster. Nobody wins alone: the team's job is to keep every ball in play for five minutes. It turns a group of strangers into a team in the time it takes to lose the first ball.
entries.best: Team days · Family zones · Schools · Exhibition stands

entries.name: SPRAY WALL
entries.line: Infrared spray cans on a digital wall: paint graffiti, or the product in your own colours, and take the picture home.
entries.moment: Pick up a can and paint. The wall is a screen, the cans are infrared, and the spray lands in real time: fat lines, drips, stencils and stamps. Guests tag a mural together, or take a car, a sneaker or a bottle and spray it in their own colours. Every piece goes home by email and the best of the day fill a gallery on the wall.
entries.best: Youth & street culture events · Auto & sneaker launches · Malls · Festivals

families.intro: A physical thing to hold, turn or step on, with a digital world behind it. The object gives the story weight and the software gives it depth. This is where our most original work lives.

cats.name: INSTRUMENTS & TANGIBLE TABLES
cats.blurb: Crafted objects that invite the hand, and reward it.

entries.name: THE TIME TELESCOPE
entries.line: Look through an antique-style telescope and watch a landmark travel through the eras of its own life.
entries.moment: A crafted scale model sits beside a brass telescope. Lean in, and the same building appears as a living, cinematic world. Turn the Era dial and the centuries click past. Turn the Zoom dial and you are standing in the courtyard. Everyone else follows the journey on a companion screen.
entries.best: Museums · Heritage sites · Tourism stands · Real-estate launches

entries.name: THE TOKEN TABLE
entries.line: Place crafted objects on a glowing table and the story assembles itself around them.
entries.moment: Pick up a token: a carved skill, a product, a district. Set it down and it introduces itself. Add a second and the table draws the connection and plays the story found where the two meet. Fill the table together for the finale, then return the tokens to their glowing docks.
entries.best: Experience centres · Education · B2B showrooms · Museums

entries.name: THE LIVING BOOK
entries.line: A real, oversized book whose pages are blank until you turn them. Then text, film and illustration bloom across the paper.
entries.moment: A great book lies open on a lectern, its pages blank. Turn one, and ink seems to flood the paper: a title writes itself, an illustration blooms, a film plays inside a frame on the page. Touch a picture and it answers. Visitors handle it like a precious volume, and it tells your story chapter by chapter.
entries.best: Museums · Visitor centres · Brand heritage rooms · Libraries & archives

entries.name: TERRAIN TABLE
entries.line: A table of fine sand. Shape it with your hands and light paints the consequences: water finds the valleys, green follows the water.
entries.moment: A broad table of fine white sand, and an open invitation to dig. Push up a ridge and it is painted as mountain; scoop a hollow and water runs in to fill it; leave it a moment and green spreads along the banks. Children understand it without a word, and it explains watersheds, wadis and masterplans better than any diagram.
entries.best: Science centres · Sustainability pavilions · Masterplan galleries · Schools programmes

entries.name: TOKEN GARDEN
entries.line: Children plant carved tokens in a garden bed, and each one blooms on the wall behind it, growing the day's shared picture.
entries.moment: A raised garden bed, a basket of carved wooden tokens and a wall of sky behind it. A child chooses one, a word, an animal or a symbol from your story, and plants it in the soil. On the wall a flower grows from that exact spot and joins the day's shared garden. By evening it is full, and it belongs to everyone who planted.
entries.best: Festivals · Children's zones · Libraries · Schools programmes

entries.name: TREASURE TOKENS
entries.line: A site-wide hunt with physical tokens. Present the right one at the right marker and the place answers with light, sound and story.
entries.moment: Every family collects a pouch of crafted tokens at the gate. Around the site stand markers, each waiting for one of them. Present the right token and the place answers: a lantern lights, a voice tells a story, a hidden carving glows. The hunt takes visitors to every corner of the site, and the tokens go home as keepsakes.
entries.best: Heritage festivals · Destinations & resorts · Museums · Family trails

entries.name: AR SLIDE TABLE
entries.line: Slide a marker across the table and detailed 3D models rise, rotate and come apart into their components.
entries.moment: A physical marker sits on a long touch table. Slide it to a chapter and a detailed model rises beside it: a turbine, a tower, an engine. Turn the marker and the model turns with it; lift it and the model comes apart into its components, each one named, then draws itself back together.
entries.best: Energy & industry stands · Real estate · Automotive · Trade shows

entries.name: CUBE CONTROL
entries.line: A real puzzle cube in your hands drives a giant glowing one in front of you.
entries.moment: Pick up the puzzle cube and twist it. In front of you a glowing cube two metres tall makes exactly the same move, face for face, in real time. Solve a side and the big cube unlocks a film, a fact or a prize. Simple to grasp and hard to put down, it turns a desk toy into a stage.
entries.best: Tech & telecom stands · Education events · Retail activations · Gaming zones

entries.name: SEAL & CEREMONY
entries.line: One crafted object carried by the host. Presented at each threshold, it wakes the room for this delegation alone.
entries.moment: The host carries a single crafted object, a seal in brass and stone. At each threshold it is set into a waiting niche, and the room wakes for this delegation alone: lights rise, the welcome appears in their language, the content turns to their interests. No tablets and no remote controls, only a gesture with the weight of ceremony.
entries.best: VIP experience centres · Government showcases · Headquarters · State visits

entries.name: COMMUNAL TABLE
entries.line: Twelve seats, twelve small screens, one host. Strangers answer playful prompts and the best answers build one shared piece on the wall.
entries.moment: Twelve seats around one long table, a small screen at each place and a host at the head. A prompt appears, a colour, a memory or a first line, and each guest writes a few words. The host gathers the best, and line by line a shared piece builds on the wall: a poem, a manifesto, a letter to the future. Strangers leave having written something together.
entries.best: Cultural evenings · Festivals · Corporate retreats · Hospitality

entries.name: THE STORY CUBE
entries.line: A cube in your hands; turn it to any face and the screen changes chapter.
entries.moment: A solid cube, beautifully made, with a symbol on each face. Set it down and the screen shows the chapter that faces up; turn it and the chapter changes, six stories in one object. It is the simplest interface in the catalogue and the most satisfying to hold, which is why people play with it longer than they read.
entries.best: Museums · Brand heritage rooms · Exhibition stands · Showrooms

entries.name: THE WHEEL
entries.line: Spin a real wheel and the screen lands on a chapter, a prize or a question.
entries.moment: A big, well-made wheel with a satisfying click. Spin it and the screen spins with it, slowing to land on a chapter of the story, a question for the quiz, or a prize. It is a game show and a menu at once, and the sound of it draws people from across the hall. Dress it in brass and timber for a heritage event or in neon for a launch.
entries.best: Exhibition stands · Promotions · Quiz nights · Retail

entries.name: HOLO TOKENS
entries.line: Pick up a small model or a glowing tube, set it on the reader, and the hologram answers with that story.
entries.moment: A row of small objects on a shelf: a model of the tower, a vial of the fragrance, a tiny turbine, a glowing tube for each theme. Choose one and place it on the reader, and the hologram beside it wakes with that object's story turning in mid-air. Six objects, six chapters, and the pleasure of choosing with your hands rather than from a menu.
entries.best: Museums · Product showcases · Energy & science pavilions · Exhibition stands

cats.name: PROJECTION MAPPING
cats.blurb: Light as a material, fitted to mountains, façades, models and tabletops.

entries.name: MOUNTAIN & FAÇADE MAPPING
entries.line: Heritage walls, towers and whole mountainsides become a night-time canvas.
entries.moment: The rock begins almost still. Lines of water appear through its cracks, tools and silhouettes emerge in gold, and the mountain tells how the place was made. We write, design and animate the film to the real surface, so the landscape stays the hero and the technology disappears into the dark.
entries.best: Cultural festivals · National celebrations · Landmarks · Destination launches

entries.name: THE PAINTED MODEL
entries.line: An immaculate white scale model brought to life by light. Turn one brass dial and the city repaints itself.
entries.moment: The model stays pure white while the film is painted onto it: districts ignite at dusk, light runs the new streets, dawn sweeps the towers. One physical dial moves between themes such as education, culture, nature and community. The film can be re-authored as the real city grows.
entries.best: Masterplans · Real-estate sales centres · City galleries · Visitor centres

entries.name: ARTISAN TABLES
entries.line: Projection on the craftsperson's own workbench shows fibre becoming weave and clay becoming vessel, without upstaging the maker.
entries.moment: The craftsperson works as she always has, and the bench around her hands quietly fills in the story. Light on the tabletop shows the palm frond becoming a strip, the strip becoming a weave, the weave becoming the basket she is finishing now. The maker stays the hero, and visitors finally see the hours hidden inside the object.
entries.best: Heritage festivals · Craft markets · Museums · Cultural pavilions

entries.name: STORY TUNNEL
entries.line: A walk-through passage where words, patterns or whole brand worlds flow across every surface around you.
entries.moment: A passage where every surface is alive. Words, patterns and images stream along the walls, across the floor and over the visitors themselves, flowing in the direction of travel like a current. It can carry a poem, a brand world or a journey through time, and it is the transition that turns arriving into being inside.
entries.best: Festival entrances · Brand worlds · Museums · Launch events

entries.name: LIVING SKETCH WALL
entries.line: Colour a character on paper, scan it, and watch it walk into the projected world alongside everyone else's.
entries.moment: Children colour a character on paper: a camel, a falcon, a dhow. They slide the page under the scanner, and seconds later their own drawing walks, flies or sails into the great projected world on the wall, crayon marks and all, alongside everyone else's. The shout of recognition is the same every time.
entries.best: Family zones · Children's museums · Malls · Festivals

entries.name: CONSTELLATION ROOM
entries.line: Ceiling and walls mapped as one slow, breathing sky. The atmosphere an entire event lives inside.
entries.moment: The whole room becomes one slow sky. Stars drift across the ceiling and down the walls, constellations draw themselves and fade, and at the key moments of the evening the sky gathers into your emblem or parts for a film. It is scenery more than spectacle: the atmosphere that an entire event lives inside.
entries.best: Gala dinners · Award nights · Employee events · Weddings

entries.name: THRESHOLD PASSAGE
entries.line: An entrance corridor that senses guests and carries light and imagery along with them as they walk.
entries.moment: The corridor is dark and still until someone steps in. Then light gathers around them and travels with them, and imagery opens along the walls at walking pace: a landscape, a history, a welcome. A second guest gets a current of their own. By the far end, everyone has been personally escorted into the experience.
entries.best: Experience centres · Museums · Headquarters · Brand homes

entries.name: SCULPTURE MAPPING
entries.line: Precise projection onto a sculpture, product or artwork, so a still object appears to change material, glow and move.
entries.moment: A white sculpture stands under a single beam and begins to change. Marble becomes bronze, bronze becomes flowing water, cracks of light run across it and heal. The object never moves, yet it seems to breathe. The same craft turns a car, a trainer or a bottle into the screen for its own story.
entries.best: Product launches · Art exhibitions · Museums · Retail windows

entries.name: TABLE STORIES
entries.line: Dining and meeting tables as canvases. Courses, chapters or data unfold across the tabletop in front of each guest.
entries.moment: The tablecloth is the screen. Before each course, the table in front of every guest comes alive: a garden grows around the plate, a tide washes in under the glasses, a tiny chef prepares the dish in miniature. For a boardroom the same table carries the plan, the map and the numbers, unfolding as the conversation does.
entries.best: Gala & state dinners · Restaurants · Boardrooms · Launch dinners

entries.name: TERRAIN IN LIGHT
entries.line: A white relief of your site and one brass button. Each press repaints the landscape with another layer of the plan.
entries.moment: A white relief model of your site, as pure as paper, and one brass button. Press it and the landscape is painted with its first layer: the water, the roads, the green. Press again for the next. In six presses a visitor has seen the entire plan, at their own pace, without a single slide.
entries.best: Masterplans · Destinations · Infrastructure projects · Visitor centres

cats.name: RESPONSIVE SURFACES
cats.blurb: Floors, walls and veils that answer the people in front of them.

entries.name: LIVING FLOOR
entries.line: A floor that sees where people walk and answers with ripples, trails and light.
entries.moment: Step onto dark water and rings of light spread from your feet. Children discover it first, then everyone is walking in patterns. The same floor becomes a game board, a map that guides guests to their seats, or a brand world that reacts to every footstep.
entries.best: Entrances · Malls · Family zones · Launch events

entries.name: THE MESSAGE CONSTELLATION
entries.line: Guests type a wish, a word or a thank-you, and it rises onto a great wall as a star in a growing constellation.
entries.moment: At a slim writing station each guest adds a few words. Their message becomes a glowing star that drifts up to join hundreds of others, until the wall holds a living portrait of the room. Every message is moderated before it appears and handed to you afterwards as a complete keepsake record.
entries.best: Employee days · National occasions · Biennales · Conferences

entries.name: STEP TILES
entries.line: Light-up pressure tiles for races, rhythm games and glowing footprints. The most energetic square metres on the floor.
entries.moment: A dance floor that keeps score. Tiles light under every footstep, and the games change through the day: chase the colour, follow the rhythm, race a friend across the grid. Between games it lies quiet, glowing softly where people cross it. Few things pull a crowd faster or photograph better.
entries.best: Malls · Retail activations · Family zones · Festivals

entries.name: TOUCH-SENSE WALL
entries.line: A printed or sculpted wall with hidden sensitivity. Touch an illustration and it answers with film, sound and light.
entries.moment: It looks like a beautifully illustrated mural, with no screens and no buttons in sight. Touch the drawing of the dhow and you hear the sea and the crew's song. Touch the pearl merchant and a film opens beside him. The whole wall is quietly alive, and discovering that is half the pleasure.
entries.best: Museums · Visitor centres · Children's hospitals · Brand heritage walls

entries.name: FLICK TO WALL
entries.line: Browse on a small touchscreen, then flick what you love onto the big wall for everyone to see.
entries.moment: Visitors browse on a small screen at their own pace: projects, products, photographs. When something catches their eye, they flick it upward, and it flies onto the big wall in front of everyone. The stand's main screen becomes a live reflection of what your visitors care about, and every flick starts a conversation.
entries.best: Trade-show stands · Showrooms · Real-estate sales · Archives

entries.name: RAIL EXPLORER
entries.line: Push a screen along a six-metre rail and it reveals the hidden layer of whatever sits behind it: a timeline, a skyline, a machine.
entries.moment: A screen rides on a long rail in front of a printed wall or a scale model. Push it along, and wherever it stops it reveals the hidden layer of what lies behind it: the year behind the date, the interior behind the façade, the working parts behind the casing. The visitor's own push drives the story, which makes it theirs.
entries.best: Timelines & heritage walls · Skylines & models · Industrial stands · Museums

entries.name: ECHO VEIL
entries.line: Layers of translucent mesh hold several ghostly versions of you at once. Stand still and they settle into one.
entries.moment: Walk towards the veil and several ghostly versions of you appear in its layers, each a little out of step with the others. Move, and they multiply. Stand perfectly still, and they drift together and settle into one. It turns a simple truth into something you feel in your own body: be still, and things come into focus.
entries.best: Science & technology pavilions · Art festivals · Innovation centres · Museums

entries.name: PATTERN WALK
entries.line: Patterned light in the floor and the canopy overlap into slow-shifting bands that visitors walk through.
entries.moment: Fine patterns of light in the floor and in the canopy overhead overlap, and between them appear slow bands that shift as you move: an effect no photograph quite captures, because it depends on where you stand. Visitors slow down without being asked. It is a passage that turns walking into looking.
entries.best: Innovation centres · Science pavilions · Atriums · Art installations

entries.name: LINKED PAIR
entries.line: Two sculptures across a hall that answer each other instantly. Touch one, and the other responds.
entries.moment: Two sculptures stand at opposite ends of the hall. Lay a hand on one, and the other answers in the same instant, with the same colour and the same pulse. Strangers on either side find themselves in a conversation of light. It works across a hall, between two buildings, or between two cities.
entries.best: Innovation centres · Twin venues & campuses · Airports · Public art

entries.name: LIVE CANVAS
entries.line: A large wall that is never a loop. Its imagery is generated live from weather, time, crowd or your own data.
entries.moment: A great wall of moving image that never repeats, because nothing on it is recorded. It paints itself live from the world around it: the wind outside, the hour, the number of people in the room, the pulse of your own data. Art-directed by us, it has a recognisable hand, and no two visits are the same.
entries.best: Headquarters lobbies · Innovation centres · Hospitality · Airports

entries.name: INSIGHT PANELS
entries.line: A calm row of gallery-framed displays turning live data into plain-language headlines.
entries.moment: A row of screens framed and hung like paintings. Each takes one stream of live data and states it as a single sentence anyone can read, with one quiet visual behind it. No dashboards and no dials. Leaders stop at them the way they would at a picture, and leave knowing the number that matters today.
entries.best: Executive floors · Command centres · Investor suites · Exhibition stands

entries.name: DRAWING WALL
entries.line: Families draw on small tablets and approved drawings join a living collective canvas on the big screen.
entries.moment: Families sit with small tablets and draw: a flower, a falcon, a house, a wish. A moderator approves each one, and it floats onto the great shared canvas on the wall, where it drifts and mingles with hundreds of others. By the end of the festival the wall is a portrait of everyone who came.
entries.best: Cultural festivals · Family zones · Community events · Museums

entries.name: REACTIVE MURAL
entries.line: An illustrated wall that stirs as people pass. Characters glance, patterns ripple, details wake.
entries.moment: An illustrated wall, drawn for your story, that seems at first to be a painting. Then a bird turns its head as you pass. Leaves stir in your wake, a lantern flickers on, a cat slips behind a doorway. Nothing demands attention and everything rewards it, so people walk the wall twice.
entries.best: Corridors & concourses · Hospitals · Schools · Hospitality

entries.name: GLASS TOUCH WALL
entries.line: A transparent surface that turns into a touch display when approached, then clears again.
entries.moment: A sheet of clear glass with the real view behind it: a showroom, a garden, a skyline. Walk up and the glass wakes, laying information over exactly what you are looking at. Touch to explore, step away and it clears. The screen is only there when somebody wants it.
entries.best: Showrooms · Observation decks · Real-estate sales · Museums

entries.name: SHADOW PLAY
entries.line: Your silhouette on the screen, dressed in effects, or clearing the smoke to reveal the clean city behind.
entries.moment: Stand in front of the wall and your shadow appears on it, larger than life. Move, and it grows wings, scatters into birds, fills with stars, or, for a sustainability story, pushes back the smoke to reveal a clean city wherever you stand. The wall reads bodies, not faces, so it works for a crowd and for a child, and it films beautifully.
entries.best: Sustainability & energy pavilions · Family zones · Malls · Festivals

entries.name: THE WATERFALL
entries.line: Stories cascade down a tall screen; touch one and it pauses to be read.
entries.moment: A tall screen where news, pictures and quotes fall like water, a slow cascade that never repeats. Touch one as it passes and it stops for you, opening into the full story while the rest keeps flowing around it. Let go and it rejoins the fall. For a lobby it is ambient and alive; for a stand it is a way to show two hundred things without a menu.
entries.best: Corporate lobbies · Exhibition stands · Newsrooms & media · Universities

entries.name: THE SMART MIRROR
entries.line: A mirror that sees you: a skeleton that moves as you move, your vitals at a glance.
entries.moment: A full-length mirror that looks back. Step onto the plate and it draws a skeleton that moves exactly as you do, then reads your height, weight and balance and lays them beside your reflection. It can coach a stretch, compare a posture, or simply amaze. For health, sport and wellness brands it is a demonstration that needs no explanation.
entries.best: Health & wellness brands · Sports events · Clinics & pharma stands · Gyms

cats.name: HOLOGRAMS & SPATIAL DISPLAYS
cats.blurb: Images that leave the screen and stand in the room with you.

entries.name: HOLOGRAPHIC CONCIERGE
entries.line: A life-size figure of light that greets guests, answers their questions and points the way, in Arabic and English.
entries.moment: The first thing a visitor meets is a host who looks at them, listens and replies. Ask for directions, ask about the programme, ask about the organisation: the answers come only from content you have approved. It turns the welcome desk into the most photographed spot at the entrance.
entries.best: Exhibition entrances · Lobbies · Museums · Airports & malls

entries.name: ANAMORPHIC CORNER
entries.line: An L-shaped screen where objects appear to float out into the room. No glasses, only the right angle.
entries.moment: Walk towards the corner and the wall seems to open into a deep niche. Artefacts, products or creatures drift out past the edge of the screen and turn in the air in front of you. We design the content from the visitor's exact viewpoint, because that is what makes the illusion hold. Shown here: our scenes for a museum's exhibition stand.
entries.best: Trade-show stands · Museum foyers · Retail windows · Outdoor screens
entries.client: AL FAHIDI FORT MUSEUM · DUBAI CULTURE

entries.name: HOLO PRESENTER
entries.line: A freestanding cabinet with a life-size presenter inside: a spokesperson, a founder, a figure from history.
entries.moment: A life-size figure stands inside a slim cabinet and speaks to the room: your chief executive welcoming visitors in three cities at once, a founder telling the story in his own words, a figure from history stepping out of the archive. Recorded in our studio or created with AI, and changed as easily as a playlist.
entries.best: Exhibition stands · Museums · Retail · Roadshows

entries.name: HOLOGRAM FAN WALL
entries.line: Spinning blades of light make logos and products hover in mid-air. Link many together for a floating wall.
entries.moment: Images that hang in the air with nothing behind them. A single unit floats a product above a counter; a wall of them, linked together, makes a trainer three metres wide turn in space above the stand. Bright, quick to install and impossible to ignore, it is the easiest way to stop a passing crowd.
entries.best: Retail · Trade shows · Malls · Product launches

entries.name: HOLO SHOWCASE
entries.line: The real product sits inside a glass case while holographic animation orbits, labels and dismantles it.
entries.moment: The real product sits inside a glass case, and light performs around it. Particles orbit the watch, a glowing line traces the movement inside, the ingredients of a fragrance rise from the bottle like smoke. The object stays the hero, and the hologram says everything the label cannot.
entries.best: Luxury retail · Museums · Product launches · Trade shows

entries.name: FLOATING HOLOGRAM
entries.line: A large mid-air image for dark rooms and stages, positioned wherever the story needs it.
entries.moment: In a dark room, a great image hangs in the air, and the audience can see straight through it: a planet turning above the stage, a whale crossing the hall, a building assembling itself beside the speaker. Performers can stand behind it and inside it. It is stage magic at the scale of architecture.
entries.best: Keynotes & launches · Opening ceremonies · Museums · Theatres

entries.name: HOLO TUBE
entries.line: A clear vertical tube with a three-dimensional figure or product turning inside.
entries.moment: A clear column with something impossible inside it: a falcon hovering mid-beat, a product turning slowly, a dancer the height of your hand. Visitors can walk all the way around and see it from every side. It needs very little floor space and works as a marker, a centrepiece or a family of pieces across a stand.
entries.best: Exhibition stands · Retail · Museums · Lobbies

entries.name: TOUCHABLE HOLOGRAM
entries.line: Holograms that respond to gesture, voice or touch, so visitors explore rather than watch.
entries.moment: The image floats in front of you, and it answers your hand. Reach out and turn the engine, pull the building apart floor by floor, spin the globe and pick a country. Nothing is touched, which keeps it clean, and everything responds, which keeps people there far longer than a film would.
entries.best: Tech & automotive stands · Science centres · Healthcare · Showrooms

entries.name: GHOST GLASS
entries.line: Sharp, lifelike visuals that seem to hang in space behind a pane of glass.
entries.moment: Behind a pane of glass, in what looks like an empty set, a figure appears: sharp, lifelike, and clearly not there. A craftsman works at a real bench, a dancer crosses a real floor, then fades. It is the oldest illusion in theatre rebuilt with today's images, and it suits stories that need a human presence.
entries.best: Museums · Heritage houses · Retail windows · Visitor centres

entries.name: SEE-THROUGH SCREENS
entries.line: Transparent displays layered over real objects, annotating whatever sits behind the glass.
entries.moment: The object sits in its case, and the glass in front of it is the screen. Labels appear beside the details they describe, a lost colour returns to a faded textile, an animation shows how the mechanism once moved. Visitors never have to choose between looking at the real thing and learning about it.
entries.best: Museums · Luxury retail · Automotive showrooms · Trade shows

entries.name: SCREEN DOORS
entries.line: Automatic sliding doors that are themselves transparent screens. The entrance becomes the first exhibit.
entries.moment: The entrance doors are clear glass, and they are also the first screen of the visit. A wave rolls across them, a welcome forms, and as a guest approaches the image parts with the doors themselves. Every arrival becomes a small reveal, and the entrance starts working before anyone is inside.
entries.best: Flagship stores · Experience centres · Museums · Headquarters

entries.name: LED CUBE & GLOBE
entries.line: Sculptural screens, a five-sided cube or a full 360° globe, steered from a touch podium.
entries.moment: A screen you can walk around. A cube suspended over the stand shows five faces of one story, or a full globe turns with the world's weather, trade routes or your global footprint on its surface. From a touch podium, visitors spin it, stop it and dive into any point.
entries.best: Exhibition stands · Lobbies · Command & visitor centres · Museums

entries.name: IMMERSIVE ROOM
entries.line: Walls, floor and ceiling of screen. Step inside the content and it responds to where you stand.
entries.moment: Step through the door and the content is no longer in front of you; it is everywhere. Walls, floor and ceiling carry one continuous world: a seabed, a forest, a city a hundred years from now. It responds to where people stand, so a group can walk together through a place that does not exist yet.
entries.best: Experience centres · Museums · Real-estate sales · Brand homes

entries.name: AMBIENT HOLOGRAM
entries.line: A small holographic vitrine looping a precious object or building, turning slowly beside the real display.
entries.moment: A small vitrine on a plinth, and inside it a precious thing made of light: a fort, a jewel, a manuscript, turning slowly. It asks nothing of the visitor. Beside a real display it shows the angle nobody can see, the building as it once stood, or the object that was too fragile to travel.
entries.best: Museums · Heritage sites · Jewellery & watches · Reception desks

entries.name: THE TRANSFORMATION MIRROR
entries.line: See yourself in the holobox, and two seconds later you are the character.
entries.moment: A tall holographic cabinet that shows you as you are, life-size. Two seconds later you begin to change: armour grows, a costume settles, a creature's features arrive, and the figure in the box is still you, still moving as you move. Choose the character from a tablet or let the box choose for you. Every transformation is filmed and sent to the guest's phone.
entries.best: Entertainment launches · Gaming & film events · Malls · Youth festivals

entries.name: HOLOGRAPHIC FAÇADE
entries.line: A transparent holographic net in front of the screen wall, so 3D figures float in front of the picture.
entries.moment: The stand's tall screen wall carries the picture; a fine transparent holographic net hangs a metre in front of it and carries the figures. Between them, three-dimensional creatures, products and shapes appear to hover in the air in front of the wall, drifting out over the heads of the crowd. Seen from the aisle the whole façade seems to have depth, which is why people cross the hall to check.
entries.best: Exhibition façades · Stage backdrops · Retail windows · Launch events

entries.name: VEIL ROOM
entries.line: A room of transparent screen mesh with a volumetric light sculpture at its heart.
entries.moment: Walls you can see through, made of transparent screen mesh, and at the centre a volumetric display, a sculpture of pure light. The walls carry colour, pattern and landscape; the centrepiece carries the three-dimensional object: a monument, a molecule, a product, a face that greets each guest. Because the walls are veils, the room stays open to the hall around it while holding its own world inside.
entries.best: Pavilions · Museums · Real-estate showcases · Product launches

entries.name: THE ASCENT
entries.line: Guests sit on a platform that lifts them into a dome in the ceiling for a one-minute journey.
entries.moment: Eight guests take their seats on a round platform. It rises, slowly, into a dome hidden in the ceiling, and the dome closes around them with picture: a flight over the coast, a dive to the reef, a journey to the site you are selling. A minute later the platform descends and the next eight step on. It is a ride, an exhibit and a queue-maker in one.
entries.best: Pavilions · Real estate & tourism · Auto shows · Experience centres

entries.name: LIVE CONFIGURATOR
entries.line: The real product behind a reflective screen; choose colour and trim on the tablet and the object itself appears to change.
entries.moment: The real product sits in a case behind a reflective screen. On the tablet, a guest chooses a colour, a finish, a trim, and the object in front of them appears to change: the paint shifts, the material turns to leather, a pattern spreads across the body. It is a configurator you can walk around, and it works for a car, a watch, a chair, a phone.
entries.best: Auto & watch brands · Furniture & design · Fashion & accessories · Retail

entries.name: THE TURNING WINDOW
entries.line: A screen on a revolving mount: turn it to look around a place that isn't there, no headset needed.
entries.moment: A screen on a stand that turns like a telescope. Swing it left and the view swings left; look up and you look up; the picture is a 360-degree film or a virtual world, and the screen is your window into it. It shows a hotel room, a museum gallery or a future street to a queue of people, one at a time, without headsets, hygiene worries or the loneliness of VR.
entries.best: Tourism & hospitality · Real estate · Museums · Trade shows

cats.name: AI ENCOUNTERS
